name: BitMob Expert 1
how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models
items.result: Pulse fields tie; 95% of reads under 22.6 ms vs 36.6; 643 MB vs 724; neighbour topic agreement 0.683 vs 0.648; chunked late-passage recall 0.859 vs 0.867

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

plain.blocker: Story type and topic are ready; the reader that serves them is now v6b-student (15 ms, one CPU thread). Condition is parked: the readers differ in strictness and the CPU reader finds about 3 in 10 real cases; which condition, direction and size wait behind it.

Two guesses: 92.2% agreement with Sonnet on the sealed set (best constant pair 38.2%); 79.9% against human labels (MN-DS, fresh articles), right at the 80% line.
Parked at the field gate after two definition rounds. v6b-student finds 29.3% of real cases and its end-to-end 86.3% is below simply saying no (89.1%). No gross false-yes errors in the outside check.
Only meaningful on articles that have a condition. 79.2%, 3 points short.
Same slice as condition; waits until condition is ready.
Waits on condition; the old score is trivial (guessing scores 97.3%).

Counted per trait, not one pass or fail: 2 of 51 traits are GO (deaths or injuries; a household price went up, revised wording). Two others failed the gate (a threat to the natural environment, a single city or smaller area). 45 need a wording revision, 2 need more positive examples. The row is Ready when you name the traits the product needs and all of them are GO.
